body: ### Description Move the rest of the state over to the state management cache layer. All state within the controller lifecycle (minus a few cases before the controller is initialized, or outside of the normal lifecycle, like resetting state) are now going through the in-memory state management layer. This also means that we unlock having differing states for cline instances, even though they are all sharing the same state storage. For example, if I switch to act mode in one Cline instance, another Cline instance is still in plan mode and can operate accordingly. That new mode value is only read from storage on initialization - once I restart Cline. ### Test Procedure Test all settings, switch to different providers and models, use Cline normally. ### Type of Change - [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) - [x] ♻️ Refactor Changes - [ ] 💅 Cosmetic Changes - [ ] 📚 Documentation update - [ ] 🏃 Workflow Changes ### Pre-flight Checklist - [x] Changes are limited to a single feature, bugfix or chore (split larger changes into separate PRs) - [x] Tests are passing (`npm test`) and code is formatted and linted (`npm run format && npm run lint`) - [ ] I have created a changeset using `npm run changeset` (required for user-facing changes) - [x] I have reviewed [contributor guidelines](https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) ### Screenshots This screen recording shows running Cline in a GitHub Codespace in the current version of production and in this branch. body:
## Unit Test Recommendations for Magero Store

This analysis provides a comprehensive list of unit tests that should be implemented for the magero-store ASP.NET Core MVC e-commerce application.

### Application Overview
The magero-store is an e-commerce web application built with ASP.NET Core MVC, featuring:
- Product catalog browsing and searching
- Shopping cart functionality with session storage
- Entity Framework data access with SQLite
- Sample data for product listings

### Recommended Unit Tests by Component

#### **1. Model Tests**

**Product Model Tests:**
- Validate required fields (Name, Price) throw validation errors when null/empty
- Validate Price accepts positive decimal values
- Validate Price rejects negative values
- Validate data annotations work correctly
- Test property getters and setters

**CartItem Model Tests:**
- Validate ProductId is properly set
- Validate Quantity accepts positive integers
- Validate Quantity rejects negative/zero values
- Test relationship between CartItem and Product
- Test default values initialization

#### **2. Controller Tests**

**HomeController Tests:**
- `Index()` returns correct view with sample products
- `Index()` returns ViewResult type
- `Error()` returns error view
- Verify products are passed to view correctly

**ProductsController Tests:**
- `Index()` without search term returns all sample products
- `Index()` with search term filters products by description
- `Index()` with empty search term returns all products  
- `Index()` with non-matching search term returns empty results
- `Details()` with valid ID returns correct product
- `Details()` with invalid ID returns NotFound
- `Search()` method handles SQL queries properly (integration test)
- Configuration dependency injection works correctly

**CartController Tests:**
- `Index()` returns cart items from session
- `AddToCart()` with valid product ID adds item to cart
- `AddToCart()` with invalid product ID returns NotFound
- `AddToCart()` with existing product increments quantity
- `AddToCart()` with new product creates new cart item
- `RemoveFromCart()` removes item from cart
- `RemoveFromCart()` with non-existent item handles gracefully
- `Checkout()` with empty cart redirects to home
- `Checkout()` with items returns checkout view
- `GetCartItems()` returns empty list when session is null
- `SaveCartItems()` properly stores items in session

#### **3. Data Layer Tests**

**ApplicationDbContext Tests:**
- DbContext initializes correctly with options
- DbSets (Products, CartItems) are properly configured
- OnModelCreating seeds initial data correctly
- Database connection string configuration works
- Entity configurations and relationships are correct

**SampleData Tests:**
- Products collection contains expected number of items
- All products have required fields populated
- Product IDs are unique
- Prices are valid positive decimals
- Image URLs are properly formatted

#### **4. Helper Tests**

**SessionExtensions Tests:**
- `Set<T>()` properly serializes objects to JSON
- `Get<T>()` properly deserializes JSON to objects
- `Get<T>()` returns default value when key doesn't exist
- `Get<T>()` handles null session gracefully
- JSON serialization/deserialization handles complex objects
- Generic type constraints work correctly

#### **5. Integration Tests**

**Cart Session Management:**
- Cart persists across requests within same session
- Multiple products can be added to cart
- Cart calculations (totals, quantities) are correct
- Cart survives page navigation
- Session timeout clears cart appropriately

**Product Search Integration:**
- Search functionality works end-to-end
- Search handles special characters safely
- Search returns relevant results
- Empty search results display properly

#### **6. Validation Tests**

**Model Validation:**
- Required field validation triggers on empty values
- Data annotation validation works correctly
- Custom validation rules function properly
- Model state validation integrates with controllers

**Input Validation:**
- Controller actions validate input parameters
- SQL injection prevention in search functionality
- XSS prevention in user inputs
- Null reference handling

#### **7. Configuration Tests**

**Dependency Injection:**
- Services are properly registered in Program.cs
- DbContext configuration works with different providers
- Session configuration is applied correctly
- Controller dependencies resolve properly

### Test Infrastructure Recommendations

Since no test infrastructure currently exists, recommend creating:
- **xUnit test project** for unit tests
- **Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing** for integration tests
- **Moq** for mocking dependencies
- **Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.InMemory** for database testing
- **FluentAssertions** for readable test assertions

### Coverage Goals
- **Controllers:** 90%+ line coverage
- **Models:** 100% property and validation coverage  
- **Helpers:** 95%+ line coverage
- **Critical paths:** Cart operations, product search, data access

This comprehensive test suite would ensure the application's reliability, maintainability, and regression prevention while supporting future feature development.

body: Fixes a critical bug where the circuit breaker ignored failed liquidation attempts by deprecating `record_market_data` for liquidation tracking and adding comprehensive tests. The `record_market_data` method's `liquidation_attempted: liquidation_occurred` logic incorrectly treated `liquidation_occurred = false` as "no attempt," failing to distinguish between failed attempts and no attempts. This PR addresses the critical monitoring blind spot by deprecating `record_market_data` for liquidation tracking, adding inline documentation, and guiding users to `record_liquidation_attempt` for accurate tracking of all attempts, while maintaining backward compatibility for pure price updates. ---

author: copilot
body:
Blog posts were being created with hardcoded partition key "sample-blog-post" instead of using the actual slug, causing all blog posts to overwrite each other in production.

## Root Cause

The `UpsertBlogPost` function has an optional slug route parameter (`Route = "posts/{slug?}"`) and falls back to using the slug from the request body when no route slug is provided. Client applications were consistently sending placeholder values like "sample-blog-post" in the JSON payload, resulting in all blog posts getting the same partition key in Azure Table Storage.

## Solution

Enhanced the slug extraction and validation logic in `UpsertBlogPost.cs`:

**1. Improved Slug Priority Logic**
- Route slug now takes clear priority over model slug
- Added detailed logging to track which slug source is being used
- Better error messages guide users on proper slug usage

**2. Placeholder Slug Detection**
Added `IsPlaceholderSlug()` method that rejects common placeholder patterns:
- `sample-blog-post`, `test-blog-post`, `example-blog-post`
- `demo-post`, `template-post`, etc.
- Case-insensitive matching

**3. Slug Format Validation**
Added `IsValidSlug()` method enforcing URL-safe format:
- Only lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens
- No leading/trailing hyphens or consecutive hyphens
- Proper alphanumeric boundaries

## Impact

**Before:**
```bash
POST /posts
Content: {"slug": "sample-blog-post", "title": "My Post"}
→ Partition Key: "sample-blog-post" (overwrites existing posts)
```

**After:**
```bash
POST /posts/my-unique-post
Content: {"title": "My Post"}
→ Partition Key: "my-unique-post" ✅

POST /posts
Content: {"slug": "sample-blog-post", "title": "My Post"}
→ HTTP 400: "Invalid slug 'sample-blog-post'. Please provide a unique, meaningful slug." ❌
```

This ensures each blog post gets a unique partition key, preventing data loss while maintaining backward compatibility for properly formatted slugs.

Fixes #30.

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When a pod is not in the default namespace, the reattach message generated after an attach session ends now includes the -n flag with the namespace name. This ensures the suggested command will work correctly for pods in non-default namespaces.

author: copilot
body:
Enhanced the file preview functionality on the app detail page to provide professional syntax highlighting using `react-syntax-highlighter` with comprehensive support for different file formats.

## Key Features

- **Images** (`image/*`): Displays actual images with dimensions and proper sizing constraints
- **JSON** (`application/json`): Interactive preview with "Pretty Print" ↔ "Show Raw" toggle and professional syntax highlighting with distinct colors for keys, values, and punctuation
- **Python** (`text/x-python*`): Professional syntax highlighting matching GitHub standards with keywords, strings, operators, and identifiers in distinct colors, plus "Format Code" ↔ "Show Original" toggle
- **Programming Languages**: Automatic language detection and syntax highlighting for JavaScript, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, SCSS, Markdown, Bash, C/C++, Java, PHP, Ruby, Go, Rust, SQL, and more
- **Text files** (`text/plain`, `text/*`): Clean plain text display with preserved formatting
- **Unsupported types**: User-friendly fallback with clear messaging, MIME type information, and download option

## Professional Syntax Highlighting

The implementation uses `react-syntax-highlighter` with the highlight.js engine and `atomOneDark` theme, providing:
- **Python**: Keywords (`def`, `print`, `if`) in purple/blue, strings in green, operators and punctuation with distinct colors
- **JSON**: Keys, values, braces, brackets, and commas each with professional color coding
- **Multi-language support**: Intelligent file extension detection with appropriate syntax highlighting
- **Clean styling**: Professional slate-800 background (`#1e293b`) that matches the app theme

## Interactive Formatting

Both JSON and Python files feature interactive formatting controls:
- **JSON Pretty Print**: Toggles between compressed raw JSON and properly formatted JSON with syntax highlighting
- **Python Code Formatting**: Provides basic code formatting with proper indentation and structure cleanup

## Technical Implementation

- Professional syntax highlighting with `react-syntax-highlighter` using highlight.js engine and `atomOneDark` theme
- Intelligent mimetype detection with `getPreviewType()` helper function
- Automatic programming language detection by file extension with `getLanguageFromFile()`
- Specialized preview components for each supported file type
- Performance optimization by skipping content fetching for images and unsupported files
- Smart loading states and error handling
- Complete backwards compatibility with existing functionality
- Proper dependency organization with `@types/react-syntax-highlighter` in devDependencies

## User Experience

- Professional code rendering matching GitHub, VS Code, and modern editor standards
- Interactive toggle buttons for formatting options
- Clear file type indicators and size information
- Graceful degradation for unsupported formats with helpful guidance
- Responsive design supporting various screen sizes

The implementation maintains full compatibility with existing file handling while significantly enhancing the preview experience with professional-grade syntax highlighting for developers working with badge applications.

Fixes #1.
